editorial_intent: Diagram how misfolded tau downregulates Kv7/Kcnq3 potassium channels in locus coeruleus neurons, causing voltage-gated ion imbalance and hyperexcitability that is reversed by channel-activating molecules.
subject: A cross-sectional noradrenergic brainstem neuron membrane depicting tau-mediated suppression of Kv7 potassium pore channels (Kcnq3/Kcnd1) alongside an restored outward positive ion vector field
setting: A background framing featuring a geometric cranial meridian dome, a 24-division circadian astrolabe calibration arc, and a phase-coherent geodesic neural constellation rendered in precision Bauhaus vector lines
composition: Asymmetric Post-Constructivist dual-panel lithograph layout showing a left-side membrane potential collapse (suppressed outward potassium flow and trapped hyperactive voltage vectors) transitioning across a central structural blockade to a right-side Kv7 channel opening stabilized by retigabine molecular vectors
